claim: Recent molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of human hemoglobin give results in disagreement with experiment.
source: Recent molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of human hemoglobin (Hb) give results in disagreement with experiment.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a direct assertion about the state of recent MD simulations.

claim: The unliganded (T0) and liganded (R4) tetramers of hemoglobin are stable in solution.
source: Although it is known that the unliganded (T0) and liganded (R4) tetramers are stable in solution, the published MD simulations of T0 undergo a rapid quaternary transition to an R-like structure.
evidence: This is stated as known experimental fact in the abstract.

claim: Published MD simulations of T0 undergo a rapid quaternary transition to an R-like structure.
source: Although it is known that the unliganded (T0) and liganded (R4) tetramers are stable in solution, the published MD simulations of T0 undergo a rapid quaternary transition to an R-like structure.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from published simulations in the abstract.

claim: T0 is stable only when the periodic solvent box contains ten times more water molecules than the standard size for such simulations.
source: We show that T0 is stable only when the periodic solvent box contains ten times more water molecules than the standard size for such simulations.
evidence: This is the main finding stated in the abstract, supported by the simulation data presented in the manuscript.

claim: A large box is required for the hydrophobic effect, which stabilizes the T0 tetramer, to be manifested.
source: The results suggest that such a large box is required for the hydrophobic effect, which stabilizes the T0 tetramer, to be manifested.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the simulation results stated in the abstract.

claim: T0 is not stable unless His146 is protonated, even in the largest box.
source: Even in the largest box, T0 is not stable unless His146 is protonated, providing an atomistic validation of the Perutz model.
evidence: This is stated as a finding in the abstract and supported by simulation data.

claim: The finding that His146 protonation is required for T0 stability provides an atomistic validation of the Perutz model.
source: Even in the largest box, T0 is not stable unless His146 is protonated, providing an atomistic validation of the Perutz model.
evidence: This is an interpretation connecting the simulation results to the Perutz model.

claim: Extra large boxes may be required to obtain meaningful results in simulations of a wide range of systems.
source: The possibility that extra large boxes are required to obtain meaningful results will have to be considered in evaluating existing and future simulations of a wide range of systems.
evidence: This is stated as a broader implication in the abstract.

claim: Human hemoglobin is the paradigmatic model system for cooperativity in proteins.
source: Human hemoglobin is the paradigmatic model system for cooperativity in proteins.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Hemoglobin transports oxygen from the lungs to the tissues.
source: It transports oxygen from the lungs to the tissues and it is composed of two identical α-chains (α1 and α2) and two identical β−chains (β1 and β2).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about hemoglobin function.

claim: Hemoglobin is composed of two identical α-chains (α1 and α2) and two identical β-chains (β1 and β2).
source: It transports oxygen from the lungs to the tissues and it is composed of two identical α-chains (α1 and α2) and two identical β−chains (β1 and β2).
evidence: This is stated as established structural knowledge about hemoglobin.

claim: The α and β chains form two identical dimers (α1β1 and α2β2).
source: They form two identical dimers (α1β1 and α2β2), whose relative orientation differs significantly in the unliganded (T0) and liganded (R4) tetramer. (Baldwin and Chothia, 1979)
evidence: This is stated as established structural knowledge with citation.

claim: The relative orientation of the dimers differs significantly in the unliganded (T0) and liganded (R4) tetramer.
source: They form two identical dimers (α1β1 and α2β2), whose relative orientation differs significantly in the unliganded (T0) and liganded (R4) tetramer. (Baldwin and Chothia, 1979)
evidence: This is stated as established structural knowledge with citation.

claim: How hemoglobin functions at the atomistic level is still not fully understood.
source: Although there is a vast literature on Hb and its cooperative mechanism (Schechter, 2008), how it functions at the atomistic level is still not fully understood (Cui and Karplus, 2008).
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap with citations.

claim: The first insight into the hemoglobin mechanism was obtained from low-resolution structures (5.5 Å) of the hemoglobin tetramer.
source: The first insight into the mechanism was obtained from the low-resolution structures (5.5 Å) of the hemoglobin tetramer (Muirhead and Perutz, 1963), which showed that the heme groups were too distant to be able to interact directly.
evidence: This is stated as historical fact with citation.

claim: The heme groups in hemoglobin are too distant to be able to interact directly.
source: The first insight into the mechanism was obtained from the low-resolution structures (5.5 Å) of the hemoglobin tetramer (Muirhead and Perutz, 1963), which showed that the heme groups were too distant to be able to interact directly.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from structural studies with citation.

claim: Monod, Wyman and Changeux formulated the allosteric (MWC) model based on the structural transition between two quaternary structures (T and R) to explain the indirect interaction between the heme groups required for cooperative oxygen binding.
source: Monod, Wyman and Changeux formulated the allosteric (MWC) model (Monod et al., 1965; Cui and Karplus, 2008) based on the structural transition between two quaternary structures (T and R) to explain the indirect interaction between the heme groups required for cooperative oxygen binding.
evidence: This is stated as historical fact about the MWC model with citations.

claim: Higher resolution (2.8 Å) X-ray structures of unliganded and liganded hemoglobin confirmed that there exist two quaternary structures (deoxy (T0) and oxy (R4)) for the tetramer and two tertiary structures for each individual chain (liganded and unliganded).
source: Higher resolution (2.8 Å) X-ray structures of unliganded and liganded hemoglobin (Perutz, 1970) confirmed that there exist two quaternary structures (deoxy (T0) and oxy (R4)) for the tetramer and two tertiary structures for each individual chain (liganded and unliganded).
evidence: This is stated as established structural knowledge with citation.

claim: Perutz proposed a stereochemical mechanism for cooperativity in which salt bridges (some with ionizable protons in the neutral pH range) provide the link between ligand-induced tertiary changes and the relative stability of the two quaternary structures.
source: Based on the structural results, as well as mutant data, Perutz, 1970) proposed a stereochemical mechanism for cooperativity, in which salt bridges (some with ionizable protons in the neutral pH range) provide the link between ligand-induced tertiary changes and the relative stability of the two quaternary structures.
evidence: This is stated as historical fact about the Perutz mechanism with citation.

claim: The elements of the Perutz mechanism were incorporated into a structure-based statistical mechanical model.
source: Shortly afterwards, the elements of the Perutz mechanism were incorporated into a structure-based statistical mechanical model (Szabo and Karplus, 1972).
evidence: This is stated as historical fact with citation.

claim: The structure-based statistical mechanical model provides a quantitative framework for the effects of specific tertiary structural changes induced by ligand binding on the relative stability of the T and R structures.
source: The model provides a quantitative framework for the effects of specific tertiary structural changes induced by ligand binding on the relative stability of the T and R structures (Szabo and Karplus, 1972; Gelin and Karplus, 1977).
evidence: This is stated as a description of the model with citations.

claim: The shift of the equilibrium from T to R as a function of ligand concentration results in the sigmoidal (cooperative) ligand binding curve.
source: The shift of the equilibrium from T to R as a function of ligand concentration results in the sigmoidal (cooperative) ligand binding curve.
evidence: This is stated as an explanation of cooperativity.

claim: Several papers using different force fields and simulation conditions have been published recently describing molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of the T and R states, including T0 and R4.
source: Several papers using different force fields and simulation conditions have been published recently (Hub et al., 2010; Yusuff et al., 2012) describing molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of the T and R states, including T0 and R4 for which 1.25 Å resolution X-ray structures are available (T0, 2DN2; R4, 2DN3) (Park et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated as a literature review with citations.

claim: 1.25 Å resolution X-ray structures are available for T0 (2DN2) and R4 (2DN3).
source: Several papers using different force fields and simulation conditions have been published recently (Hub et al., 2010; Yusuff et al., 2012) describing molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of the T and R states, including T0 and R4 for which 1.25 Å resolution X-ray structures are available (T0, 2DN2; R4, 2DN3) (Park et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated as established structural data with citation.

claim: R4 was found to be stable for several hundred nanoseconds in published MD simulations.
source: Although R4 was found to be stable for several hundred nanoseconds, the T0 state was not.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from published simulations.

claim: The T0 state was found to make a transition to an R-like state in several hundred nanoseconds in published MD simulations.
source: It was found to make a transition to an R-like state in the same time period (see also Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from published simulations and referenced to a figure.

claim: The rate of the T0 to R0 transition has not been measured directly.
source: Although the rate of the T0 to R0 transition has not been measured directly, it can be estimated from the experimentally determined R0 to T0 transition rates and the R0/T0 equilibrium constant.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap.

claim: For the unliganded hemoglobin tetramer, the R0 to T0 rate is about 20 μs.
source: For the unliganded hemoglobin tetramer, the R0 to T0 rate is about 20 μs (Sawicki and Gibson, 1976).
evidence: This is stated as experimental data with citation.

claim: There is a striking disagreement between the transition time observed in the simulations and the estimate from experiment.
source: There is, thus, a striking disagreement between the transition time observed in the simulations and the estimate from experiment.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion comparing simulation and experimental results.

claim: The hydrophobic effect arises from the disruption of the bulk water hydrogen bond network around nonpolar groups.
source: In search for an answer, we focused on the hydrophobic effect (Chothia et al., 1976; Lesk et al., 1985), which arises from the disruption of the bulk water hydrogen bond network around nonpolar groups (Rossky et al., 1979; Cheng and Rossky, 1998).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: For large molecules, there is a 'dewetting' phenomenon that stabilizes a more compact structure.
source: The theoretical analysis of Chandler and coworkers (Chandler, 2005; Chandler and Varilly, 2012) indicated that for large molecules, there was a 'dewetting' phenomenon that stabilizes a more compact structure.
evidence: This is stated as a theoretical result with citations.

claim: A larger surface area is buried in deoxy- than in methemoglobin as a result of tertiary and quaternary structure changes.
source: Chothia et al. (1976) noted that "A larger surface area is buried in deoxy- than in methemoglobin as a result of tertiary and quaternary structure changes. [..] This implies that hydrophobicity stabilizes the deoxy structure, the free energy spent in keeping the subunits in a low-affinity conformation being compensated by hydrophobic free energy due to the smaller surface area accessible to solvent.'
evidence: This is stated as a finding from Chothia et al. with citation.

claim: Hydrophobicity stabilizes the deoxy structure, the free energy spent in keeping the subunits in a low-affinity conformation being compensated by hydrophobic free energy due to the smaller surface area accessible to solvent.
source: Chothia et al. (1976) noted that "A larger surface area is buried in deoxy- than in methemoglobin as a result of tertiary and quaternary structure changes. [..] This implies that hydrophobicity stabilizes the deoxy structure, the free energy spent in keeping the subunits in a low-affinity conformation being compensated by hydrophobic free energy due to the smaller surface area accessible to solvent.'
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation from Chothia et al. with citation.

claim: Such a stabilizing effect of T0 should appear naturally in a MD simulation, but evidently did not do so in the published simulations.
source: Such a stabilizing effect of T0 should appear naturally in a MD simulation, but evidently did not do so in the published simulations (Hub et al., 2010; Yusuff et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as an observation about published simulations with citations.

claim: The standard box used was 75 Å with 10,763 water molecules, as well as enough Na+ and Cl− ions to yield a 0.15 m/L molar concentration.
source: The box we first used was 75 Å; the T0 tetramer dimensions are approximately 54×49×50 Å, and there were 10,763 water molecules, as well as enough Na+ and Cl− ions to yield a 0.15 m/L molar concentration.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the simulation setup.

claim: The T0 tetramer dimensions are approximately 54×49×50 Å.
source: The box we first used was 75 Å; the T0 tetramer dimensions are approximately 54×49×50 Å, and there were 10,763 water molecules, as well as enough Na+ and Cl− ions to yield a 0.15 m/L molar concentration.
evidence: This is stated as a structural measurement.

claim: All MD simulations were done in the NPT ensemble.
source: All MD simulations were done in the NPT ensemble (see SI for details).
evidence: This is stated as a methodological detail.

claim: 1 μs simulations were carried out with four cubic boxes: 75 Å (10,543 water molecules), 90 Å (20,756 water molecules), 120 Å (53,287 water molecules), and 150 Å (105,073 water molecules).
source: To investigate the possibility that larger boxes were required for stabilizing T0, we carried out 1μs simulations with four cubic boxes, 75 Å (10,543 water molecules) 90 Å (20,756 water molecules), 120 Å (53,287) and 150 Å (105,073), see Figure 1—figure supplement 1.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the simulation setup with reference to a figure.

claim: In all simulations with different box sizes, His146β1 and His146β2 were protonated.
source: In all these simulations, His146β1 and His146β2, which play an essential role in the Perutz model (Perutz, 1970), were protonated.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological detail with citation.

claim: His146β1 and His146β2 play an essential role in the Perutz model.
source: In all these simulations, His146β1 and His146β2, which play an essential role in the Perutz model (Perutz, 1970), were protonated.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.

claim: T0 is stable for the entire simulation in the 150 Å box.
source: The essential result is that T0 is stable for the entire simulation in the 150 Å box, while it is not in the smaller boxes (for details, see SI).
evidence: This is stated as the main finding from the simulations.

claim: T0 is not stable in the smaller boxes (75, 90, and 120 Å).
source: The essential result is that T0 is stable for the entire simulation in the 150 Å box, while it is not in the smaller boxes (for details, see SI).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the simulations.

claim: The structure at the end of the 90 Å box simulation is more similar to the oxy R4 structure (2DN3) than to the deoxy T0 structure (2DN2).
source: Figure 2 shows the structures obtained at the end of the 1 μs simulations, superposed on the X-ray structure that is more similar; that is, the oxy R4 structure (2DN3) for the 90 and 120 Å simulations and the deoxy T0 structure (2DN2) for the 150 Å box simulation (see also Table 1).
evidence: This is stated as a result with reference to a figure and table.

claim: The structure at the end of the 120 Å box simulation is more similar to the oxy R4 structure (2DN3) than to the deoxy T0 structure (2DN2).
source: Figure 2 shows the structures obtained at the end of the 1 μs simulations, superposed on the X-ray structure that is more similar; that is, the oxy R4 structure (2DN3) for the 90 and 120 Å simulations and the deoxy T0 structure (2DN2) for the 150 Å box simulation (see also Table 1).
evidence: This is stated as a result with reference to a figure and table.

claim: The structure at the end of the 150 Å box simulation is more similar to the deoxy T0 structure (2DN2) than to the oxy R4 structure (2DN3).
source: Figure 2 shows the structures obtained at the end of the 1 μs simulations, superposed on the X-ray structure that is more similar; that is, the oxy R4 structure (2DN3) for the 90 and 120 Å simulations and the deoxy T0 structure (2DN2) for the 150 Å box simulation (see also Table 1).
evidence: This is stated as a result with reference to a figure and table.

claim: Such small energy differences (10^-4 kcal/mol per water molecule) are very difficult to capture in MD simulations.
source: Such small energy differences are very difficult to capture in MD simulations and is not attempted here.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of MD simulations.

claim: The decrease in average number of hydrogen bonds per water molecule is consistent with the estimated energy change per water molecule.
source: This is consistent with the estimated energy change per water molecule.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the simulation results.

claim: The fluctuation of <NH−bonds>/molecule decreases with increasing box size.
source: Furthermore, Figure 3 demonstrates that the fluctuation of <NH−bonds>/molecule decreases with increasing box size which is the behaviour expected from statistical mechanics.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the simulations with reference to a figure.

claim: The decrease in fluctuation of <NH−bonds>/molecule with increasing box size is the behavior expected from statistical mechanics.
source: Furthermore, Figure 3 demonstrates that the fluctuation of <NH−bonds>/molecule decreases with increasing box size which is the behaviour expected from statistical mechanics.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation connecting the observation to statistical mechanics.

claim: The running averages of <NH−bonds>/molecule were evaluated over time intervals between which transitions were observed.
source: It should be pointed out that the running averages were evaluated over time intervals between which transitions were observed, see Figure 1.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological detail with reference to a figure.

claim: For the largest box studied by Yeh and Hummer (40 Å) the size correction was negligible.
source: For the largest box they studied (40 Å) the size correction was negligible.
evidence: This is stated as a result from Yeh and Hummer.

claim: The calculated self-diffusion coefficient from MD simulations with Hb present is identical to that of pure water only for the largest 150 Å box.
source: However, the calculated self-diffusion coefficient from MD simulations with Hb present, is identical to that of pure water only for the largest 150 Å box.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the simulations.

claim: There is a linear relationship between the calculated D-value for boxes containing Hb and the time in ns when the first transition from the T0 structure takes place.
source: In Figure 4B, we plot the calculated D−value for boxes containing Hb versus the time in ns when the first transition from the T0 structure takes place. As can be seen, there is a linear relationship between the two.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the simulations with reference to a figure.

claim: An extrapolation of the line relating D-value to transition time indicates that in the 150 Å box, the first transition away from T0 should take place at 700 ns.
source: Of most interest is the fact that an extrapolation of the line indicates that in the 150 Å box, the first transition away from T0 should take place at 700 ns.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the linear relationship.

claim: In the 150 Å box, T0 is still present at 1.4 μs.
source: However, we have shown that in the 150 Å box, T0 is still present at 1.4 μs.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the simulations.

claim: The fact that T0 is still present at 1.4 μs in the 150 Å box provides strong evidence that T0 is in fact stable in a 150 Å box.
source: This provides strong evidence that in a 150 Å box, T0 is in fact stable.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the simulation results.

claim: The linear dependence between D-value and transition time was not expected.
source: This linear dependence was not expected.
evidence: This is stated as a comment on the finding.

claim: The origin of the linear dependence between D-value and transition time still requires explanations at a molecular level.
source: It is an interesting result whose origin, though, still requires explanations at a molecular level.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap.

claim: Simulations for all box sizes have been done with His146 deprotonated.
source: Simulations for all box sizes have also been done with His146 deprotonated.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological detail.

claim: With His146 deprotonated, T0 is stabilized in larger boxes, but after less than 100 ns a transition to an R-like state occurs.
source: The results for that system showed that T0 is stabilized in larger boxes, but after less than 100 ns a transition to an R-like state occurs.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the simulations.

claim: The finding that T0 transitions to R-like state with His146 deprotonated provides direct evidence that His146 protonation is essential for stabilizing T0.
source: This provides direct evidence that His146 protonation is essential for stabilizing T0, in accord with the Perutz model (Perutz, 1970).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the simulation results with citation.

claim: The finding that His146 protonation is essential for stabilizing T0 is in accord with the Perutz model.
source: This provides direct evidence that His146 protonation is essential for stabilizing T0, in accord with the Perutz model (Perutz, 1970).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation connecting the simulation results to the Perutz model with citation.

claim: Chandler showed that significant water depletion around a spherical hydrophobic solute is expected when its radius is larger than 1 nm (10 Å).
source: To relate the above results to the hydrophobic effect, we use the construct of Chandler (Chandler, 2005), who showed (Figure 5A) that significant water depletion around a spherical hydrophobic solute is expected when its radius is larger than 1 nm (10 Å).
evidence: This is stated as a result from Chandler with citation and reference to a figure.

claim: Hb is nearly spherical with a 2.8 nm radius.
source: Since Hb is nearly spherical with a 2.8 nm radius, we calculated the g(r) for the 90 and 150 Å box (see Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated as a structural property of Hb.

claim: The behavior of g(r) in the 150 Å box is consistent with the expected water structuring.
source: The behavior in the 150 Å box is consistent with the expected water structuring, while for the 90 Å box it is not.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the simulations.

claim: The behavior of g(r) in the 90 Å box is not consistent with the expected water structuring.
source: The behavior in the 150 Å box is consistent with the expected water structuring, while for the 90 Å box it is not.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the simulations.

claim: The structural transitions are accompanied by pronounced dewetting and water penetration.
source: Furthermore, the structural transitions are accompanied by pronounced dewetting and water penetration as shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 4 for the 90 Å box.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the simulations with reference to a figure.

claim: The T0 state is only found to be thermodynamically stable if the hydration water behaves like bulk water as judged from the self-diffusion coefficient.
source: To summarize, the T0 state is only found to be thermodynamically stable if (i) the hydration water behaves like bulk water as judged from the self-diffusion coefficient, (ii) the number of hydrogen bonds per water molecule is large enough and its fluctuation around the average sufficiently small, see Figure 3—figure supplement 1.
evidence: This is stated as a summary conclusion from the simulations.

claim: The T0 state is only found to be thermodynamically stable if the number of hydrogen bonds per water molecule is large enough and its fluctuation around the average sufficiently small.
source: To summarize, the T0 state is only found to be thermodynamically stable if (i) the hydration water behaves like bulk water as judged from the self-diffusion coefficient, (ii) the number of hydrogen bonds per water molecule is large enough and its fluctuation around the average sufficiently small, see Figure 3—figure supplement 1.
evidence: This is stated as a summary conclusion from the simulations.

claim: If water is not engaged in an adequate number of water-water H-bonds, solvent water is prone to attack the protein salt bridges, destabilizing them and eventually to break them.
source: Therefore, if water is not engaged in an adequate number of water-water H-bonds, solvent water is prone to attack the protein salt bridges, destabilizing them and eventually to break them.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the mechanism.

claim: For the 150 Å box the g(r) around His146 remains almost invariant.
source: For the 150 Å box the g(r) remains almost invariant whereas for the 120 Å box an appreciable change occurs during the time when the major structural transition at 920 ns takes place.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the simulations.

claim: For the 120 Å box an appreciable change in g(r) around His146 occurs during the time when the major structural transition at 920 ns takes place.
source: For the 150 Å box the g(r) remains almost invariant whereas for the 120 Å box an appreciable change occurs during the time when the major structural transition at 920 ns takes place.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the simulations.

claim: For the smallest boxes, the local g(r) around His146 is very variable.
source: For the smallest boxes, the local g(r) is very variable, which supports the importance of locally structured water molecules for stabilizing the T0 state.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the simulations.

claim: The variability of local g(r) around His146 in smallest boxes supports the importance of locally structured water molecules for stabilizing the T0 state.
source: For the smallest boxes, the local g(r) is very variable, which supports the importance of locally structured water molecules for stabilizing the T0 state.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the simulation results.

claim: For the largest box, the parameters examined (e.g. the salt bridge to Lys40) fluctuate around the equilibrium values near those of the T0 structure.
source: The results (Figure 1—figure supplement 3–5) show that for the largest box, the parameters examined (e.g. the salt bridge to Lys40, discussed by Perutz) fluctuate around the equilibrium values near those of the T0 structure while for the smaller boxes there are abrupt changes, correlated with global structural transitions.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the simulations with reference to figures.

claim: For the smaller boxes there are abrupt changes in local structural parameters, correlated with global structural transitions.
source: The results (Figure 1—figure supplement 3–5) show that for the largest box, the parameters examined (e.g. the salt bridge to Lys40, discussed by Perutz) fluctuate around the equilibrium values near those of the T0 structure while for the smaller boxes there are abrupt changes, correlated with global structural transitions.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the simulations with reference to figures.

claim: The transition away from the T0 structure extends over approximately 10 ns.
source: The transition away from the T0 structure extends over approximately 10 ns during which several important contacts are broken or formed, see Figure 1—figure supplement 5A.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the simulations with reference to a figure.

claim: The apparent activation energy from the simulations in the smaller solvent boxes is near zero.
source: This value suggests that the apparent activation energy from the simulations in the smaller solvent boxes is near zero, in contrast to an estimate on the order of seconds for the transition if the barrier arose from the 7 kcal/mol difference in stability.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the transition time.

claim: The ability of the 150 Å box to stabilize the T-state starting from the R-like structure in the 120 Å box after 1 μs was explored.
source: Importantly, the ability of the 150 Å box to stabilize the T-state starting from the R-like structure in the 120 Å box after 1 μs was also explored.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological detail.

claim: Solvating the R-like structure from the 120 Å box in the 150 Å box and following the equilibrium dynamics for 1 μs, the final RMSD compared to the 2DN2 (T-state) structure is 1.97 Å.
source: Solvating this structure in the 150 Å box, minimizing, heating and equilibrating it (see Materials and methods) and following the equilibrium dynamics for 1 μs, the final RMSD compared to the 2DN2 (T-state) structure is 1.97 Å (2.55 compared to 2DN3 (R-state)) starting from an RMSD of 2.73 Å (with respect to 2DN2) and 1.42 Å (2DN3) at the beginning of the simulation (after heating and equilibration), respectively.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the simulations.

claim: The His146β1–His146β2 and His143β1–His143β2 distances change from values typical for an R-state structure to approach separations indicative of a T-state structure without fully completing the transition.
source: Concomitantly, the His146β1–His146β2 and His143β1–His143β2 distances change from values typical for an R-state structure (both ∼12.6 Å) to 14.0 Å (for His143) and 18.0 (for His146) and approach separations indicative of a T-state structure (18.6 Å and 30.9 Å) without, however, fully completing the transition to a T-state structure.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the simulations.

claim: The R0 to T0 transition time is about 20 μs, much longer than the simulation time.
source: As mentioned above, the R0 to T0 transition time is about 20 μs, much longer than the simulation time.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison between experimental and simulation timescales.

claim: The present result that much larger boxes than those used standardly are required for the hydrophobic effect to be manifested is of general interest.
source: Given the increasing use of molecular dynamics simulations to study conformational transitions in large proteins and in an explicit solvent environment, the present result that much larger boxes than those used standardly are required for what appears to be the hydrophobic effect to be manifested is of general interest.
evidence: This is stated as a broader implication of the findings.

claim: The finding has wide ranging implications for the interpretation and validity of previous simulations, as well as those to be undertaken in the future.
source: It has wide ranging implications for the interpretation and validity of previous simulations, as well as those to be undertaken in the future.
evidence: This is stated as a broader implication of the findings.

claim: The magnitude of the box size effect is expected to depend on the size (and shape) of the molecule and its hydrophobicity, as well as possibly other properties.
source: Given that the magnitude of the effect is expected to depend on the size (and shape) of the molecule and its hydrophobicity, as well as possibly other properties (Chandler, 2005), the requirement for the use of larger boxes in simulations will have to be investigated in each case.
evidence: This is stated as a speculation about the generality of the findings with citation.

claim: The requirement for the use of larger boxes in simulations will have to be investigated in each case.
source: Given that the magnitude of the effect is expected to depend on the size (and shape) of the molecule and its hydrophobicity, as well as possibly other properties (Chandler, 2005), the requirement for the use of larger boxes in simulations will have to be investigated in each case.
evidence: This is stated as a recommendation for future simulations.

claim: Capturing the correct diffusional dynamics of the environment will play a crucial role in atomistic simulations for the crowded conditions that exist in entire cells or parts thereof.
source: One particularly relevant situation where capturing the correct diffusional dynamics of the environment will play a crucial role is that in atomistic simulations for the crowded conditions (Feig et al., 2017) that exist in entire cells or parts thereof (Zhou et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated as a speculation about the implications for cellular simulations with citations.

claim: Possible errors in molecular dynamics simulation results for other phenomena, such as protein folding, as well as for polymeric materials more generally have to be considered.
source: Possible errors in molecular dynamics simulation results for other phenomena, such as protein folding, for example, as well as for polymeric materials more generally have to be considered as well.
evidence: This is stated as a speculation about the broader implications of the findings.

claim: The influence of solvent layers on the structural stability of hemoglobin tetramer was investigated using Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations.
source: The influence of solvent layers on the structural stability of hemoglobin tetramer is investigated using Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the study in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Extended large-scale simulation were performed with the CHARMM36 all atom force-field and the TIP3P water model using version 5.1.4 of the GROMACS package on GPUs.
source: Extended large-scale simulation were performed with the CHARMM36 all atom force-field (Best et al., 2012) and the TIP3P water model (Jorgensen et al., 1983) using version 5.1.4 of the GROMACS package (Abraham et al., 2015) on GPUs.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological detail with citations.

claim: The coordinates of the starting structure are taken from the X-ray structure of tetrameric human hemoglobin in the deoxy form, PDB code 2DN2 (1.25 Å resolution).
source: The coordinates of the starting structure are taken from the X-ray structure of tetrameric human hemoglobin in the deoxy form, PDB code 2DN2 (1.25 Å resolution) (Park et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated as a methodological detail with citation.

claim: The protonation states of the histidines were based on the 2013 study of Zheng et al. and the terminal β histidines (His146) were both doubly protonated.
source: The protonation states of the histidines were based on the 2013 study of Zheng et al. and the terminal β histidines (His146) were both doubly protonated (Zheng et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as a methodological detail with citation.

claim: The protein was solvated in four different cubic boxes of increasing size: 75, 90, 120 and 150 Å.
source: The protein was solvated in four different cubic boxes of increasing size: 75, 90, 120 and 150 Å.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological detail.

claim: The system was neutralized by adding counter ions and the salt concentration of 0.15 m/L was achieved using Na+ and Cl−.
source: The system was neutralized by adding counter ions and the salt concentration of 0.15 m/L was achieved using Na+ and Cl−.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological detail.

claim: The LINCS algorithm was used for constraining bonds involving H-atoms.
source: The LINCS algorithm (Hess et al., 1997) was used for constraining bonds involving H-atoms.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological detail with citation.

claim: Each system was first energy minimized for 50,000 steps using steepest descent.
source: Each system was first energy minimized for 50,000 steps using steepest descent, heated from 0 to 300 K in increments of 10 K in NVT for 300 ps, followed by 500 ps (NVT) and 500 ps of NpT equilibration at p=1 atm with a time step of 2 fs.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological detail.

claim: The center of mass of the protein was restrained to the center of mass of the simulation box.
source: The center of mass of the protein was restrained to the center of mass of the simulation box.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological detail.

claim: The Velocity Rescaling and Parrinello-Rahman methods were used for temperature and pressure control, respectively.
source: The Velocity Rescaling (Bussi et al., 2007) (with τ=0.1 ps) and Parrinello-Rahman (Parrinello and Rahman, 1981) methods were used for temperature and pressure control, respectively.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological detail with citations.

claim: The velocity rescaling method is an extension of the Berendsen thermostat to which a stochastic force chosen such as to generate a correct canonical distribution is added.
source: The velocity rescaling method is an extension of the Berendsen thermostat to which a stochastic force chosen such as to generate a correct canonical distribution is added (Bussi et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated as a methodological explanation with citation.

claim: The MD simulations for all systems were carried out for at least 1 μs at constant temperature and pressure (NpT) at 300 K and one atm with a time step of 2 fs.
source: The MD simulations for all systems were carried out for at least 1 μs at constant temperature and pressure (NpT) at 300 K and one atm with a time step of 2 fs and the 1σ temperature fluctuations over the 1 μs trajectories were 0.1 K for the 150 Å box and 0.5 K for the 90 Å box.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological detail.

claim: The 1σ temperature fluctuations over the 1 μs trajectories were 0.1 K for the 150 Å box and 0.5 K for the 90 Å box.
source: The MD simulations for all systems were carried out for at least 1 μs at constant temperature and pressure (NpT) at 300 K and one atm with a time step of 2 fs and the 1σ temperature fluctuations over the 1 μs trajectories were 0.1 K for the 150 Å box and 0.5 K for the 90 Å box.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the simulations.

claim: Water self-diffusion coefficients D were calculated for box sizes 75, 90, 120 and 150 Å, in the presence and in the absence of Hb, over the entire 1 μs trajectory.
source: Water self-diffusion coefficients D were calculated for box sizes 75, 90, 120 and 150 Å, in the presence and in the absence of Hb, over the entire 1 μs trajectory.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological detail.

claim: In the absence of the protein, the simulation boxes contained pure water systems (no ions were included).
source: In the absence of the protein, the simulation boxes contained pure water systems (no ions were included).
evidence: This is stated as a methodological detail.

claim: Including ions at physiological concentrations will typically change the water self-diffusion coefficient by 1% to 2%.
source: Including ions at physiological concentrations will typically change the water self-diffusion coefficient by 1% to 2% (Kim et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.
